en: The *Rāvaṇa-bhāṣita-kumāra-roga-pratikāra-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of the Western Heaven,
Minister Dharma-xian, Grand Master of Luminous Teaching, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
and Grand Officer of the Third Rank, under Imperial Decree.
At that time, Rāvaṇa observed all children in the world from their birth until they reached the age of twelve.
Furthermore, while they remain in a state of childish ignorance and folly,
their vital spirit is insufficient, providing an opportunity for ghosts and demons to take advantage.
There are twelve planetary mother-ghosts who roam throughout the world.
Day and night they constantly watch for an opportunity,
whether during sleep or while walking or sitting alone;
at such times, they manifest various different forms.
They terrify infants, causing them to lose their composure;
they suck away their vital essence,
whereby diseases arise and they eventually perish in infancy.
Seeing this matter, I feel profound compassion.
I shall now explain for you the twelve lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*) and their presiding mother-spirits,
as well as the symptoms of the ailments that afflict children according to the year, month, day, and hour of their birth.
Furthermore, I shall explain the methods for healing through great mantras,
up to and including the ritual procedures for performing rites and generating offerings.
If there should be anyone who hears what I have spoken, [they shall attain success].
When there are those afflicted by illness,
the vidyādhara who relies upon my teachings to provide healing and exerts sincere devotion will certainly obtain lightness, peace, happiness, and auspiciousness.

The names of the twelve lunar mansion mother-demons (*mātṛ-graha*) are as follows: first, Mātṛṇanā; second, Susuṇḍanā; third, Revatī; fourth, Mukhamaniṣkā; fifth, Vinālī; sixth, Śakunī; seventh, Bhūtānā; eighth, Śuṣkagā; ninth, Arīyakā; tenth, Rāmbhakā; eleventh, Bili-bhañjikā; twelfth, Skandā.
Regarding these twelve planetary mother-demons (*mātṛkā*),
who seize and possess young children in order to seek offerings,
I shall now describe for each of them the signs and symptoms of their possession.
Furthermore, if an infant is possessed on its first day of birth, its first month of birth,
or its year of birth, it is seized by the mother-spirit Mātṛṇanā.
That child had previously suffered from alternating chills and fevers;
his body became emaciated and gradually withered away,
his mind grew distracted and disordered, and his body was constantly trembling.
Regarding "weeping and not eating":
the Vidyādhara takes earth from the banks of two rivers and fashions the image of an afflicted child.
Within the maṇḍala of the four directions,
place an image of a child facing west.
Furthermore, arrange various kinds of incense and flowers within the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, provide white food and drink, even including wine and meat.
Again, arrange seven seats for banners and light seven lamps.
Additionally, use white mustard seeds, wild fox dung, cat dung, agallochum incense, and snake skin.
Using such medicines as these, together with ghee from a yellow cow,
blend them to form an incense and burn it to fumigate the child.
Furthermore, use sesame oil and seeds of the *śyāmā* plant.
Alternatively, one may use leaves and the leaves of the pippala tree, along with the varaṅga medicinal herb;
having thus decocted these five medicines in water, one bathes the child while reciting the Great Mantra.
Consecrate the sacrificial food and various articles within the aforementioned maṇḍala by reciting the great mantra:

*Oṃ namo rāvaṇāya trālarucye vidarabhaṇāya hana vārīṇa prahaṃma nandinna marīkarubhiṇa matrinanna vara vara śuṣka śuṣka muñca muñca kumārakaṅga svāhā*. Having thus consecrated them with the recitation of this great mantra, exit from the city.
At midday, facing east,
one should offer sacrifice to the female spirit Mātṛnandā;
all sacrificial food, incense, flowers, and other items should be discarded wherever they may be.
May the ailment of this child be swiftly cured.
Furthermore, regarding a child who falls ill on the second day after birth,
in the second month, or in the second year:
This child is possessed by the yakṣiṇī Sutanā.
Previously, the child suffered from alternating chills and fevers and exhibited signs of mental agitation;
now, with eyes closed and refusing food, he clenches his hands and feet, suffers abdominal pain, vomits, and gasps for breath.
The vidyādhara should take one *droṇa* of rice flour and fashion an image of the sick child facing west,
placing it within the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, within the maṇḍala, one should arrange various kinds of exquisite incense, flowers, food, drink, wine, meat, and so forth.
Additionally, one should employ four white banners and light four lamps upon four seats.
Furthermore, use guggulu incense, garlic, snake skin, white mustard seeds, and cat excrement mixed with clarified butter to blend into an incense paste and burn it to fumigate the child.
Also, as before, use water infused with these five medicinal substances to bathe the child.
Then, reciting the Great Mantra,
he consecrated the sacrificial food and various other items within the aforementioned maṇḍala, and spoke the Great Mantra as follows:

Oṃ namo rāvaṇāya trāḷugye vidarapāṇāya jvalanahasadharīṇi jvāle ta-has-tāya hana hana naha naha tṛśulena nuṣṭa-gṛhāṇa nikṛtaya nikṛtaya juṣaya juṣaya hana hana sunanamunca munca kumārakaṅga svāhā. Having thus recited this great mantra and empowered [it], he went outside the city.
At the hour of the Dog (19:00–21:00), facing west,
one should make offerings to the mother-demon Sūnā.
All sacrificial food, incense, flowers, and other items should be discarded wherever they may be.
May the ailment of this child be swiftly cured.
Furthermore, regarding children who fall ill on the third day after birth,
in the third month, or in the third year:
If a child is seized by the yakṣiṇī Rīvadī,
the infant will suddenly become startled and agitated,
crying out and weeping, with pain throughout the body.
Experiencing fluctuating chills and fevers, with the head and face trembling;
looking upon one's own body, gradually becoming emaciated and weak;
losing all desire for food and drink until one becomes withered and thin.
The Vidyādhara should employ various kinds of superior meat, raw meat, raw fish, wine, and so forth.
He should set up eight red banners and light eight lamps.
Furthermore, take the leaves of the *vimalā* tree, *guggulu* resin, snake skin, garlic, cat dung, white mustard seeds, and so forth;
mix these together with clarified butter (*ghṛta*) and burn them as incense for the child.
Also, boil the aforementioned five medicines together with water.
Having bathed the child, one should recite the Great Mantra (*mahāvidyā*).
Consecrate the sacrificial food and various other items as described above within the maṇḍala.
Then, recite the Great Mantra as follows:

Oṃ namo rāvaṇāya daśavadanāya jambhakahāsāya prajvalitahastāya hana hana daha daha maraya maraya nuṣṭa gṛhṇa moṭaya moṭaya svāhā. Having thus recited this great mantra (*mahāvidyā*) and empowered [the site], he went outside the city.
At the hour of the Dog (19:00–21:00), facing north,
one should sacrifice to the mother-spirits and ghosts;
all sacrificial foods and various other items should be discarded in whatever location is available.
May the ailments of the child be swiftly cured.
Furthermore, regarding children who fall ill on the fourth day after birth,
in the fourth month, or in the fourth year:
This child is possessed by the mother-demon Mūkapāṇika.
Previously, the child suffered from alternating chills and fever,
coughing, wheezing, vomiting, trembling of the body, and drooping of the head.
If one weeps, scratches both eyes with their hands, looks about at people's faces,
has no desire for food or drink, and passes frequent stools and urine,
the vidyādhara should take earth from both banks of a river.
Fashion an image of a child afflicted by illness and place it within the western section of the maṇḍala;
furthermore, arrange various kinds of incense and flowers.
Furthermore, use raw and cooked meats, as well as wine, fruit, and so forth.
Also employ four red banners, four seats, and light four lamps.
Additionally, use cotton seeds, snake skin, cat dung, cow horn, tiger claws, white mustard seeds, and the like.
Burn the same *huáiwéi* incense to fumigate the child.
Furthermore, use the aforementioned five medicinal waters to bathe the child,
while reciting the Great Mantra (*mahāvidyā*).
Having consecrated the sacrificial food and various other items within the aforementioned maṇḍala,
he then recited the great mantra (*mahāvidyā*):

*Oṃ namo bhagavate vipannumahiṣvarāya sakaṇa-hūta-śanā mukha-maṇikāya hana hana maraṇaya maraṇaya nikṛtaya nikṛtaya kha hi kha hi bhagavati mukha-maṇikāya svāhā.* Having thus recited the mantra and performed the consecration, he departed from the city.
At the hour of the Dog (Wu-shi), facing south,
one should offer sacrifice to the mother-spirit Mūkanikā.
All sacrificial foods and various articles should be discarded wherever they may be.
May the ailments of the child be swiftly cured.
Furthermore, regarding children who fall ill on the fifth day after birth, in the fifth month, or in the fifth year:
This child is possessed by the mother-demon Vināḷikā;
previously, the child suffered from a disturbed mind and frequently broke out in fits of rage.
Fever and chills fluctuate irregularly; there is coughing, wheezing, and vomiting.
Sores suddenly break out on the body, appearing like clusters of water blisters.
The eyes gaze vacantly into space, and one has no desire for food or drink.
If [the practitioner] gradually becomes emaciated and the abdomen sinks until it is no longer visible,
the vidyādhara should prepare white food, drink, wine, meat, and the like;
he should set up five white banners, light five lamps, and offer various kinds of incense, flowers, and so forth.
Furthermore, take frankincense, garlic, snake skin, cat dung, white mustard seeds, and so forth;
mix these together with clarified butter and burn them as incense to fumigate the child.
Furthermore, use the same five medicinal waters as before to bathe the child,
while reciting the Great Mantra.
Consecrate the sacrificial food and various other items within the maṇḍala as described above.
Then he spoke the great mantra:

Oṃ namo rāvaṇāya trailokyavijarāpanāya vinatke vinatke mocaya mocaya hana hana jvala hase na muñca muñca vinatke svāhā. Having thus recited the mantra and performed the consecration, he went outside the city.
At midday, facing west, one should offer oblations to the *vināyaka-mātṛkā* spirits;
all kinds of sacrificial food and other items should be discarded wherever they may be.
May the ailments of these children be swiftly cured.
Furthermore, regarding those children who fall ill on the sixth day, the sixth month, or the sixth year after their birth:
This child is possessed by the *śetakuṇḍī* mother-ghosts;
the infant first suffers from alternating chills and fevers, laughs or cries,
trembles in body, and emits a foul odor.
Regarding one who has lost their appetite for food and drink and gradually becomes emaciated:
the vidyādhara should take one *droṇa* of rice flour and fashion an image of the afflicted child.
On the western side of the maṇḍala,
further arrange various kinds of incense, flowers, food, drink, wine, meat, milk porridge,
and so forth. Furthermore, set up four white banners and four oil lamps.
Furthermore, take benzoin, garlic, snake skin, cat excrement, white mustard seeds, and ghee;
blend them together to form an incense and burn it to fumigate the child.
Additionally, use water mixed with these same five medicines as described above to bathe the child.
Then, reciting the Great Mantra,
one consecrates the sacrificial food and various articles within the aforementioned maṇḍala.
The Great Mantra is as follows:

Oṃ namo bhagavate rāvaṇāya laṅkūśvarāya vīradattaputrāya vajrahānaha na ha na śakunimuncamunca kumārakaṃ svāhā. Having thus recited this great mantra and empowered [the site], he went outside the city.
At the hour of the Dog (19:00–21:00), facing south,
one should perform the offering to the Kūṇī-mother spirits.
All sacrificial foods and various articles should be discarded wherever they may be.
May the ailment of this child be swiftly cured.
Furthermore, regarding those who fall ill on the seventh day, the seventh month, or the seventh year after the child's birth:
This child is possessed by the female spirit Pūtana.
Previously, the infant suffered from chills and fever, bodily pain,
frequent bowel movements, and constantly clenched both hands.
Regarding one who does not desire food or drink and gradually becomes emaciated:
the vidyādhara should fashion an image of the afflicted child out of *śara* grass and place it facing west within the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, one should employ various red flowers, as well as prepare red-colored foods, drinks, wine, meat, and so forth.
One should also set up eight white banners and light eight lamps.
Furthermore, one should use安息香 (bānxīxiāng), snake skin, human hair, tiger claws, leaves of the *nimba* tree, cat excrement, white mustard seeds, and clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
Combine the same ingredients to form incense and burn it before the child.
Then, as before, use the water of the five medicinal herbs to bathe the child,
while reciting the Great Mantra.
Having consecrated the sacrificial food and various other items within the aforementioned maṇḍala, he then recited the great mantra (mahāvidyā), saying:
Oṃ namo bhagavate rāvaṇāya laṅkūśvarāya vīradattaputrāya kumāragrahāya nirkṛtu hana hana jvala jvala svāhā. Having thus recited the mantra and performed the consecration, he went outside the city.
At the hour of the Dog (19:00–21:00), facing west,
one should offer sacrifice to the *bhūtanī* demoness.
All sacrificial foods and various articles should be discarded wherever they may be.
May the illness of the child be swiftly cured.
Furthermore, regarding those who fall ill on the eighth day, the eighth month, or the eighth year after the child's birth:
This child is possessed by the yakṣiṇī named Śuṣkagarmukhī.
Previously, the child suffered from alternating chills and fever;
he manifested signs of agitation and his body was in pain.
If one’s eyes cannot see objects, the head hangs low with lack of strength,
the body emits a foul odor, and one has no desire for food or drink,
the vidyādhara at that time shall take one *do* of rice flour.
Prepare one black ram and place its head facing west within the maṇḍala. Furthermore, offer incense,
flowers, milk-gruel, choice foods and drinks, as well as wine, meat, and so forth.
Furthermore, set up five white banners and light five lamps.
Additionally, use安息香 (guggulu), *sajjarasa*, snake skin, garlic, white mustard seeds, cat excrement, clarified butter (*ghṛta*), and so forth.
Grind these together to form incense and burn it before the child.
Furthermore, use the same five medicinal herbs as previously mentioned to bathe the child with water while reciting the Great Mantra.
Having consecrated the sacrificial food and various other substances within the aforementioned maṇḍala,
he then recited the great mantra (*mahāvidyā*):

Oṃ namo rāvaṇāya | trailokyavijayābhañjanāya | jvala jvala | prajvala prajvala | hana hana | hūṃ phaṭ svāhā || Having thus recited the mantra and performed the consecration, he departed from outside the city.
At the hour of the Dog (19:00–21:00), facing south,
one should offer sacrifice to the mother-demon Śuṣkagātrī.
All sacrificial foods and various other items should be discarded wherever they may be.
May the ailment of this child be swiftly cured.
Furthermore, regarding children who fall ill on the ninth day after birth, in the ninth month, or in the ninth year:
This child is possessed by the yakṣiṇī Āryakāmātṛ.
Previously, the child suffered from alternating chills and fever;
his body trembled, he wept, and his entire body was in pain.
Spitting out froth from the mouth with incessant vomiting;
perhaps with the head and neck drooping or the eyes rolling back;
and having no desire for food or drink.
The Vidyādhara takes one *droṇa* of rice flour and fashions a white ram;
he then anoints the ram with white incense.
Place the head toward the west within the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, arrange various kinds of incense, flowers, superior food and drink, wine, meat, and so forth.
Additionally, set up four white banners and light four oil lamps.
Furthermore, use snake skin as incense to fumigate the child. Also,
bathe the child with the same five medicinal waters as mentioned previously,
while reciting the Great Mantra.
Having empowered the sacrificial food and various other items within the aforementioned maṇḍala, he then recited the great mantra (*mahāvidyā*):
*Oṃ namo laṅkādhipataye laṅkeśvarāya hana hana paca paca hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Having thus recited the mantra and performed the empowerment, he went outside the city.
At the hour of the Dog (19:00–21:00), facing north,
one should make offerings to the *ariyaka* mother-spirits.
All sacrificial food and various other items should be discarded wherever they may be.
May the ailment of this child be swiftly cured and healed.
Furthermore, regarding children who fall ill on the tenth day after birth, in the tenth month, or in the tenth year:
This child was seized by the rākṣasī named Rañjaka-mātḥ;
the child had previously suffered from alternating chills and fever,
and suddenly began making evil sounds and vomiting incessantly.
One will frequently pass urine and feces,
suffer greatly from eye ailments and dental problems,
and have no desire for food or drink.
Then the vidyādhara takes earth from both banks of the river and fashions small images of children.
He applies ox-gall (*gorocanā*) to the images and places them facing west within the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, one should provide various kinds of incense, flowers, and food and drink of superior flavor, including wine, meat, and so forth.
Additionally, one should employ安息香 (aloe wood), chicken wings, ox horns, snake skins, human bone, cat excrement, white mustard seeds, and ghee.
Burn the same *saman* as incense to fumigate the child.
Furthermore, use the aforementioned five medicinal waters to bathe the child,
while reciting the Great Mantra.
Having empowered the sacrificial food and various articles within the aforementioned maṇḍala, he then recited the great mantra:
*Oṃ namo bhagavate vāsundharāya ramaṇavimalebhyaḥ hana hana ghaṭa svāhā*. Having thus recited the mantra and performed the empowerment, he departed from the city.
At the hour of the Dog (wu-shi), facing south,
one should sacrifice to the mother-demon Rāvaṇaka.
All sacrificial foods and various offerings should be discarded wherever they may be.
May the ailments of the child be swiftly cured.
Furthermore, regarding those who fall ill on the eleventh day after birth, the eleventh month, or the eleventh year:
This is seized by the Kāpālika spirits;
the child previously suffered from chills and fever,
with his body trembling and pain in the joints of his fingers.
Weeping, vomiting, and refusing food and drink,
gazing upward at the void while gradually wasting away— when such occurs,
the vidyādhara should fashion an image of the afflicted child using one *droṇa* of powdered black beans.
Having anointed one's face with red sandalwood incense, sit peacefully within the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, arrange various kinds of incense, flowers, food, drink, wine, meat, and so forth,
divided into twenty-five portions.
Set up twenty-five banners and burn twenty-five lamps.
Furthermore, use pigeon dung, the wings of a pigeon or a dove, human hair, the horn of a black goat, cat dung, and white mustard seeds mixed with ghee.
Burn the same *saman* as incense to fumigate the child.
Furthermore, use the aforementioned five medicinal waters to bathe the child,
while reciting the Great Mantra.
Having empowered the sacrificial food and various other items within the aforementioned maṇḍala, he then recited the great mantra (*mahāvidyā*):

Oṃ namo bhagavate rāvaṇāya caṇḍarohasavajragrahasadya jvala-jvala prajvala-prajvala hana-hana nṛtya-gṛha-svāhā. Having thus recited the great mantra and performed the empowerment, he went outside the city.
At the hour of the Dog (19:00–21:00), facing west,
one should make offerings to the Kumbhāṇḍa spirits.
All sacrificial foods and various articles should be discarded wherever they may be.
May the ailments of the child be swiftly cured and eliminated.
Furthermore, regarding children who fall ill on the twelfth day, the twelfth month, or the twelfth year after their birth:
This child is possessed by the yakṣiṇī Sakeṇḍā.
Previously, the child suffered from alternating chills and fever;
he glared at people with angry eyes, and according to his fixed schedule, he seized people, clutching their hands and feet as well as their bellies.
When [the victim] gradually becomes emaciated and has no desire for food or drink,
the vidyādhara should fashion an image of a child out of barley flour.
Within the maṇḍala facing west, further arrange various kinds of incense,
flowers, and offerings of superior flavors such as food, drink, wine, and meat; additionally,
set up eight red banners and light four lamps.
Furthermore, take cow horn, white mustard seeds, benzoin, garlic, snake skin, cat excrement, ghee, and so forth;
blend these together to form an incense and burn it to fumigate the child.
Additionally, use water infused with the same five aforementioned medicinal substances to bathe the child.
Then, reciting the Great Mantra,
one consecrates the sacrificial food and various other items within the aforementioned maṇḍala.
The Great Mantra is as follows:

Oṃ namo rāvaṇāya | trailokyavinaśanāya | nanta-ratkarāra | vasurāya | jana-rahasya | hana-hana | maraṇa-maraṇa | nani-na | vidrāpaya-vidrāpaya | skandha | muñca-muñca | kumāra-khaṅga | hūṃ hūṃ | phaṭ phaṭ svāhā || Having thus recited this great mantra and performed the consecration, he went outside the city.
At the hour of the Dog (戌), rotate through the four directions starting from the east and offer sacrifices to the *khandaroha* mātṛ spirits;
all sacrificial food and various other items should be discarded wherever they fall.
"May the ailment of this child be swiftly cured.
At that time, Rāvaṇa, having finished reciting this Sūtra for the Treatment of Children's Diseases, [concluded].
They withdrew with joy.
This concludes the *Rāvaṇa-bhāṣita-bāla-roga-pratikāra-sūtra* (The Sutra Spoken by Rāvaṇa on the Treatment of Childhood Diseases).
